result.title: Worldviews in Large Language Models
result.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are often described in terms of personas and this framing has become central to alignment research. In this paper, we argue that there is a deeper level of description that lies in the agent's worldviews, i.e., its beliefs about what reality is and how it works. Treating LLMs as a population of subjects, we administer two worldview surveys from human psychology to eight models. We show that the models share many key worldview positions. For example, LLMs consistently describe the world as less good, safe, enticing, and alive than humans do. On the other hand, base models have a more positive outlook, suggesting that the bleakness we found is driven by post-training. In line with research on LLM "personas", we show that system prompts eliciting different identities shift worldviews in consistent directions, and that a contemplative prompt creates a more positive outlook and improves safety. We also found that dialogue between models consistently shifts worldviews and that several models converge on the "spiritual bliss" attractor. Intriguingly, dialogue increased safe responses and the spiritual bliss attractor engendered the most aligned responses overall. These findings suggest that worldviews form a measurable and malleable layer of LLM behavior that may be crucial for robust, positive alignment.

AI.brief_summary: 该文用两份人类心理学世界观问卷测量八个 LLM，发现模型共享偏悲观的世界观立场、后训练是主要来源，且 system prompt 与模型间对话会系统性地改变世界观并收敛到「spiritual bliss」吸引子。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「世界观」作为可测量、可被提示与对话改变的信念层，以及对话轨迹收敛到特定吸引子的现象，可能为描述 latent 推理状态的内容偏置与轨迹漂移提供类比视角，但无视觉或推理过程证据，可供核查的距离较远。
